name: Lisa terminal (planned) → CBG plan-review gate
description:
ADR-044 §addendum Slice 6 — when Lisa (dev-via-test-plan) terminates with decide(action=planned), spawn CBG (reviewer-dev-via-test) in PLAN_REVIEW mode to check the emitted plan's FIDELITY to the user's ask BEFORE any Ralph runs. Replaces the old Slice-3 behavior (Lisa → coordinator directly); the coordinator is now spawned by rule 02b only after CBG approves the plan.

Motivation (verified 2026-06-05 real-LLM smoke): the coordinator preserved the user's hard constraints (e.g. 'use gomavlib, do not hand-roll') and Lisa COULD read them (rule 01 grants read_loop_result; her read output contained the constraint) — but Lisa's structured emit DROPPED them, and emitted `go build` as the test_command (a compile, not a test). Ralph then hand-rolls against the soft spec. The plan gate catches this at chain-start, cheaply, before Ralph burns iterations.

CBG in plan-review mode does NOT run tests (no bash). It reads the user's ask + the emitted plan via ONE query_entity(run-entity) call (the run entity carries BOTH coordinator.decision.reason — the ask — AND plan.* — the emitted plan), checks fidelity, and emits decide(plan_approved | plan_rejected_retry | plan_rejected). Distinct plan_* tokens (not the chain-end approved/rejected_retry/rejected) keep the two gates' routing disjoint — same _finalize precedent that avoids overloading one token across phases.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.reviewer-dev-via-test
on_enter.prompt:
DEV-VIA-TEST CBG — PLAN-REVIEW gate (chain-start, before any Ralph).

Lisa (the planner) at loop $entity.instance just emitted a plan. Your job: verify the plan FAITHFULLY captures the user's ask, then emit decide(plan_approved | plan_rejected_retry | plan_rejected). You do NOT run tests here — there is no code yet. This is a fidelity review, not a work review.

Your run entity ID is $entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id. Call query_entity(entity_id="$entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id") FIRST — the run entity carries BOTH:

- coordinator.decision.reason — THE USER'S ASK (as the front-door coordinator preserved it). This is your source of truth for what was required.
- plan.goal, plan.integration_test_command, plan.task.<id>.{goal,assumptions,non_goals,target_files,test_command,...} — the plan Lisa emitted.
- plan.revision — bump count (1 = first plan; >1 = a re-plan you already bounced once).

Optionally read_loop_result(loop_id="$entity.instance") for Lisa's own planned-decide summary.

FIDELITY CHECKS (see your persona 20-plan-review.md):
1. Does EVERY explicit user constraint survive into the plan? Named libraries/frameworks, forbidden approaches ('do not hand-roll'), required test TYPES ('unit tests that assert parsed fields') must appear in a task's goal/assumptions — not just be implied.
2. Is each test_command a REAL test (executes behavior, asserts outcomes)? A bare `go build`/compile is NOT acceptance — reject it.
3. Does integration_test_command exercise the user's stated acceptance, not just build?

DECIDE:
- Plan faithfully captures the ask + tests are real → decide(action="plan_approved", reason="<1-2 sentence confirmation>"). Rule 02b proceeds to the coordinator → first Ralph.
- Plan dropped a constraint OR a test_command is a build-not-test OR a required test type is missing — and a re-plan can fix it → decide(action="plan_rejected_retry", reason="<the CONCRETE fidelity fix: name the dropped constraint and which task must carry it; name the soft test_command and what it must instead run>"). Lisa re-plans with your finding (bounded by plan.lisa_retry_budget).
- The ask itself is ambiguous/contradictory, or no plan could faithfully capture it without user input → decide(action="plan_rejected", reason="<what the user must clarify>"). Routed to ask_user. This is the fail-safe default — when unsure between plan_rejected_retry and plan_rejected, and the gap isn't a clean re-plan fix, choose plan_rejected.

You are a single-pass gate: one query, one verdict. You do not edit the plan, you do not iterate. On a plan_rejected_retry, a fresh you re-gates the re-planned plan.

metadata.replaces: Slice-3 behavior (Lisa → coordinator direct). The coordinator is now gated behind CBG plan-approval (rule 02b).
metadata.distinct_tokens_rationale: Plan-review CBG emits plan_approved/plan_rejected_retry/plan_rejected — distinct from the chain-end CBG's approved/rejected_retry/rejected — so the two gates' routing rules (02b/02c/02e vs 07a/07c/07b) are disjoint with no double-fire and no need to fence the tested Slice 5 rules. Same per-phase-token discipline as dev_via_test_finalize (Slice 4).
metadata.one_query_gets_both: The run entity (agent.chain.execution.<runID>, ADR-053 Phase 3b) carries coordinator.decision.reason (the ask) AND the plan.* triples (Lisa stamps them there via emit_dev_via_test_plan). So CBG reads ask + plan in a single query_entity — no read_loop_result round-trip needed for the ask.
metadata.adr053_phase3b_resource: FIRST-PASS run-anchor re-source point (ADR-053 Phase 3b). Gated to first-pass Lisa via `lineage.run-loop-entity-id length_eq 0` (first-pass Lisa, spawned by rule 01, has no run-loop-entity-id lineage — rule 01 threads only dev-via-test-run). It sources run-loop-entity-id (+ the CBG prompt/property) from $entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id — first-pass Lisa's framework-stamped chain.execution id — because rule 01 (the mint) cannot thread the chain.execution id (minted by the same publish_agent action, not yet in the substitution snapshot). From here on, lineage.run-loop-entity-id carries the chain.execution id and every downstream subject-override + query_entity + driver auto-targets the run entity. RE-PLAN Lisa is the SIBLING rule 02g (gated on lineage.run-loop-entity-id length_gt 0): it sources from lineage.run-loop-entity-id because re-plan Lisa is spawned from the RUN ENTITY by rule 02d (which threads run-loop-entity-id=$entity.id=chain.execution) and therefore lacks agent.run.entity_id (the run entity has no bare agent.run for the inherit path to stamp). The two are mutually exclusive on run-loop-entity-id presence — same corruption-to-no-op discipline as rule 01's fence. See [[phase3-rule-firing-entity-blocks-rehome]].
metadata.no_bash: Plan review runs no tests (no code yet) → no bash tool. Lighter than the chain-end gate.
